flashcard_questions.q: What is a motif in film music?
flashcard_questions.a: A short, recurring musical idea representing a character, place or idea.
A motif consistently linked to one character, object or idea throughout a work.

flashcard_questions.q: Which composer's operas gave us the term leitmotif?
For which Star Wars film was The Imperial March composed?
Which character does The Imperial March represent?
flashcard_questions.a: Darth Vader and the Galactic Empire.

flashcard_questions.q: Which tonality does The Imperial March use?
Which instrument family plays the melody of The Imperial March?
Which rhythm gives The Imperial March its military character?
flashcard_questions.a: A march-like rhythm in duple time.

flashcard_questions.q: Who composed the score for The Lord of the Rings?
How many distinct themes did Howard Shore write across the trilogy?
Which tonality does the Fellowship Theme use?
Which instrument plays the rising melody of the Fellowship Theme?
How does Shore change the Fellowship Theme once the fellowship is divided?
flashcard_questions.a: He plays only a fragment on a solo instrument at a quiet dynamic.
Changing a musical idea by altering elements such as rhythm or key.

notes: 15 cards: 3 term-to-definition cards (motif, leitmotif, thematic development) with the motif and leitmotif fronts kept distinct so they do not interfere, 1 origin card (Wagner), 6 cards on the Imperial March (composer, film and year, character, tonality, instrument family, rhythm) and 4 on the Fellowship Theme (composer, number of themes, tonality, horn melody, how it is varied). The MAD T SHIRT list was left out as it would only give an enumeration answer.
